sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: A CORRIDOR OF CYCLONIC FLOW IS EXPECTED TO REMAIN ACROSS THE NRN TWO-THIRDS OF THE CONUS TODAY AS A STRONG MID-UPPER LEVEL TROUGH/ CLOSED LOW MOVES ESEWD ACROSS WRN CANADA AND THE NRN ROCKIES TO MT. STRONGEST MIDLEVEL WINDS WILL BE ATTENDANT TO THIS TROUGH WITH 60-75 KT WLY WINDS SPREADING INTO THE NRN HIGH PLAINS BY 12Z TUESDAY. MEANWHILE...A LEAD SHORTWAVE TROUGH IS EXPECTED TO MOVE THROUGH THE UPPER OH/TN VALLEYS THIS AFTERNOON AND THEN TRACK NEWD INTO NEW ENGLAND MONDAY NIGHT. FARTHER W...A SHORTWAVE TROUGH... CURRENTLY MOVING EWD ACROSS THE CENTRAL ROCKIES PER WATER VAPOR IMAGERY WILL AMPLIFY SOME AS IT MOVES ESEWD ACROSS THE CENTRAL PLAINS/OK...WITH FURTHER AMPLIFICATION EXPECTED AS THIS FEATURE REACHES MO/AR BY 12Z TUESDAY. A MIDLEVEL IMPULSE CURRENTLY LOCATED OVER SERN NM/FAR W TX IS EXPECTED TO TRACK ENEWD THROUGH W TX TO THE RED RIVER VALLEY...AND SHOULD PHASE WITH THE SRN EXTENT OF THE PLAINS TROUGH THIS AFTERNOON/TONIGHT. IN THE LOW LEVELS...A WEAK COLD FRONT WILL MOVE SLOWLY EWD THROUGH THE SRN/LOWER GREAT LAKES REGION AND OH/TN VALLEYS...WHILE THE TRAILING EXTENT OF THIS BOUNDARY SHOULD REMAIN QUASI-STATIONARY FROM SRN MO WWD TO ALONG THE OK/KS BORDER. W/NWLY MID-UPPE

sections.title: CENTRAL/SRN PLAINS EWD TO SRN MO/AR
sections.text: A VERY MOIST AIR MASS IS ALREADY IN PLACE ACROSS THE SRN PLAINS TO THE ERN HALF OF KS AND EWD TO THE OZARKS/LOWER MS VALLEY. SLY WINDS DEVELOPING OVER WRN KS BY START OF THE FORECAST PERIOD WILL ADVECT MOISTURE NWWD WITH SURFACE DEWPOINTS IN THE LOWER-MID 60S EXPECTED TO REACH NWRN KS THIS AFTERNOON. EXTENSIVE CLOUD SHIELD ASSOCIATED WITH A CLUSTER OF TSTMS CURRENTLY TRACKING EWD ALONG THE RED RIVER VALLEY MAY TEND TO LIMIT SURFACE HEATING ACROSS MUCH OF OK INTO THE EARLY AFTERNOON. HOWEVER...SURFACE HEATING ALONG THE FRONT /VICINITY OF OK/KS BORDER/ AND NWWD THROUGH KS E OF THE DRY LINE TO FAR NERN CO/SWRN NEB COMBINED WITH ERN EXTENT OF STEEP MIDLEVEL LAPSE RATES WILL SUPPORT MODERATE INSTABILITY. DESPITE LIMITED SURFACE HEATING OVER OK...DESTABILIZATION MAY BE STRONGER GIVEN HIGHER SURFACE DEWPOINTS /70S F/ WITH VERY STRONG INSTABILITY POSSIBLE /MLCAPE AROUND 3000 J PER KG/. CONVERGENCE ALONG THE AFOREMENTIONED SURFACE BOUNDARIES AND ANY OUTFLOW BOUNDARIES LEFT OVER FROM SUNDAY NIGHT/EARLY MONDAY MORNING TSTM CLUSTERS SHOULD BE THE FOCI FOR NEW TSTM DEVELOPMENT TODAY. INCREASING DEEP LAYER SHEAR THROUGH THE DAY ACROSS THE SLIGHT RISK AREA AND AVAILABLE INSTABILITY SUGGESTS ORGAN

sections.title: OH/TN VALLEYS
sections.text: THE AIR MASS IS EXPECTED TO REMAIN MOIST AND BECOME MODERATELY UNSTABLE ACROSS MUCH OF THIS REGION SUPPORTING AFTERNOON CONVECTION. THE TIMING OF THE LEAD SHORTWAVE TROUGH MOVING INTO THE UPPER OH VALLEY BY EARLY AFTERNOON AND AWAY FROM THE DESTABILIZING AIR MASS SUGGESTS LIMITED FORCING FOR ASCENT AND UNCERTAINTY IN THE OVERALL SEVERE WEATHER THREAT. GIVEN HEIGHT RISES ACROSS MUCH OF THE WEAK COLD FRONT...UPDRAFTS SHOULD NOT BE TOO ROBUST...AND THUS THE SEVERE PROBABILITIES HAVE BEEN LOWERED FROM WHAT WAS FORECAST IN THE PREVIOUS OUTLOOKS.

sections.title: SERN STATES
sections.text: A MODERATELY UNSTABLE AIR MASS...BUT WEAKLY SHEARED SUGGESTS PULSE-TYPE STORMS WILL BE POSSIBLE ACROSS MUCH OF THE CENTRAL GULF COAST STATES INTO THE SERN STATES...WITH STRONG DOWNBURST WINDS BEING THE PRIMARY THREAT.

sections.title: ERN MT/WRN ND
sections.text: A STRONGLY FORCED COLD FRONT WILL PROGRESS EWD THROUGH ERN MT INTO THE WRN DAKOTAS THIS EVENING/TONIGHT...WHERE MAINLY WEAK INSTABILITY IS EXPECTED IN THE PRE-FRONTAL AIR MASS. ALTHOUGH FORCING FOR ASCENT SHOULD PRODUCE A LINE OF TSTMS ALONG THE FRONT...THE WEAK INSTABILITY OVER ERN MT WILL LIMIT THE SEVERE WEATHER THREAT THIS EVENING. FORECAST SOUNDINGS OVER WRN ND SUGGEST POTENTIAL FOR MODERATE ELEVATED INSTABILITY LATER TONIGHT/EARLY TUESDAY...BUT A STABLE BOUNDARY LAYER MAY LIMIT STRONG WINDS FROM REACHING THE SURFACE. ..PETERS/GRAMS.. 07/12/2010

sections.title: THERE IS A SLGT RISK OF SVR TSTMS OVER ERN MT AND ND
sections.text: ...SYNOPSIS... LOW AMPLITUDE CYCLONIC FLOW ONCE AGAIN WILL PREVAIL FROM THE NRN GRT BASIN/NRN RCKYS ACROSS THE MS AND OH VLYS INTO THE MID ATLANTIC STATES/NEW ENGLAND...S OF STRONG UPR LOWS NOW OVER BC AND HUDSON BAY. THE BC LOW WILL MOVE ESE INTO SRN SK BY THE END OF THE PERIOD AS A POTENT SHORTWAVE TROUGH NOW CROSSING VANCOUVER ISLAND SWEEPS ESE INTO WRN/NRN MT. THE HUDSON BAY LOW APPEARS TO BE WEAKENING ATTM AND SHOULD FURTHER WEAKEN AS IT RETREATS N INTO NRN ONT. THIS SHOULD ALLOW HEIGHTS TO REBOUND SLIGHTLY OVER THE MID MS AND OH VLYS. SHORTWAVE RIDGING DOWNSTREAM FROM BC LOW WILL...HOWEVER...SERVE TO AMPLIFY UPR IMPULSE NOW EXTENDING FROM CNTRL MT TO CNTRL CO. THIS FEATURE SHOULD REACH THE DAKOTAS/NEB/KS BY EVE...AND IA/MO/ERN OK EARLY TUE. AT THE SFC...WEAK COLD FRONT ASSOCIATED WITH HUDSON BAY SYSTEM WILL CONTINUE SLOWLY SE ACROSS THE GRT LKS/OH VLY...AND BECOME STNRY OVER MO/ERN KS. THE WRN PART OF THE BOUNDARY ALREADY HAS BEGUN TO REFORM NWD AS A WARM FRONT ACROSS ERN WY/MT. THE BOUNDARY SHOULD CONTINUE N/NE INTO THE CNTRL DAKOTAS BY EARLY TUE AS LEE TROUGH STRENGTHENS OVER NRN HI PLNS...AND COLD FRONT ASSOCIATED WITH BC LOW ACCELERATES E INTO NW ND.

sections.title: CNTRL/SRN PLNS INTO OZARKS THIS AFTN THROUGH TONIGHT
sections.text: CONSIDERABLE DIURNAL DESTABILIZATION WILL OCCUR TODAY ALONG AND S OF AFOREMENTIONED COLD/STNRY FRONT IN MO/KS...WHERE AXIS OF HIGH PW /1.75 - 2.00 INCHES/ WILL PERSIST. IN WAKE OF OVERNIGHT STORMS...STRONG INSTABILITY ALSO SHOULD DEVELOP FARTHER NW... INVOF LEE TROUGH/OUTFLOW BOUNDARY REMNANTS AND ALONG ERN EDGE OF EML OVER WRN PARTS OF KS/NEB. POCKETS OF CONVERGENCE ALONG THE AFOREMENTIONED BOUNDARIES SHOULD PROVIDE THE MAIN FOCI FOR NEW TSTM DEVELOPMENT TODAY...WITH MODEST DEEP ASCENT PROVIDED BY AFOREMENTIONED UPR IMPULSE DRIFTING ESE FROM WY/CO. SUFFICIENT DEEP SHEAR WILL BE PRESENT FOR SUSTAINED STORMS AND FEW SUPERCELLS...ESPECIALLY FROM NE CO/SW NEB SSE TO THE OK/KS BORDER. LARGE HAIL...LOCALLY DMGG WINDS AND A TORNADO OR TWO WILL BE POSSIBLE. THE STORMS LIKELY WILL MERGE INTO A FEW CLUSTERS OVER SRN KS...SRN MO...OK...AND AR THIS EVE. FORWARD-PROPAGATING SEGMENTS MAY EXTEND THE THREAT FOR DMGG WIND/SVR HAIL INTO TONIGHT GIVEN EXPECTED INCREASE IN SSWLY LLJ AHEAD OF BC/MT UPR TROUGH.

sections.title: MT INTO WRN/CNTRL DAKOTAS THIS AFTN THROUGH EARLY TUE
sections.text: SATELLITE/GPS PW DATA SHOW SUFFICIENT MOISTURE /VALUES AROUND 1 INCH/ IN PLACE TO SUPPORT STRONG STORMS OVER ERN MT. MOISTURE SHOULD CONTINUE TO SPREAD NWD INTO ERN MT AND THE WRN DAKOTAS THROUGH THIS EVE...AS SLY LLJ STRENGTHENS AHEAD OF BC TROUGH. COMBINATION OF INCREASING MOISTURE WITH SFC HEATING AND ASCENT ALONG LEE TROUGH MAY SUPPORT A ROUND OF ISOLD TO WDLY SCTD TSTMS OVER ERN MT AND PERHAPS WRN SD THIS AFTN. THERMODYNAMIC SETUP IN THESE AREAS COULD SUPPORT A FEW INSTANCES OF GUSTY WINDS/MARGINALLY SVR HAIL. A MORE SUBSTANTIAL SVR THREAT MAY DEVELOP OVER PARTS OF THE REGION TONIGHT THROUGH EARLY TUE AS ASCENT INCREASES WITH CONTINUED EWD MOTION OF UPR TROUGH. SUSTAINED WAA/MOISTURE INFLOW AHEAD OF TROUGH...AND ...IN TIME...LOW LVL UPLIFT ALONG COLD FRONT...SHOULD SUPPORT NEW STORM DEVELOPMENT ALONG AND POSSIBLY AHEAD OF FRONT. THIS ACTIVITY MAY EVOLVE INTO A LINE OR CLUSTER...WITH AN ATTENDANT THREAT FOR DMGG WIND/HAIL.

sections.title: OH/TN VLYS THIS AFTN
sections.text: MODERATE INSTABILITY WILL DEVELOP OVER THIS REGION TODAY...BENEATH BENEATH RESIDUAL BELT OF ENHANCED WLY FLOW ON SRN FRINGE OF HUDSON BAY LOW. HOWEVER...FORCING FOR ASCENT...BOTH ALOFT AND AT LWR LVLS...WILL BE WEAK IN WAKE OF UPR IMPULSE NOW IN OH. WHILE A FEW STRONG STORMS/STORM CLUSTERS MAY EVOLVE IN POCKETS OF GREATEST LOW LVL HEATING...OVERALL SVR POTENTIAL SHOULD REMAIN FAIRLY LOW.

sections.title: NH...WRN/NRN ME THIS AFTN
sections.text: A FEW STRONG STORMS WITH MARGINALLY SVR HAIL/GUSTY WINDS MAY FORM IN ZONE OF STRONG SFC HEATING ATOP LOW LVL MOIST AXIS IN NH/WRN ME LATER TODAY. WEAK SHEAR AND WEAK FORCING FOR ASCENT SHOULD LIMIT STORM SUSTENANCE/OVERALL SVR THREAT. ..CORFIDI/ROGERS.. 07/12/2010

sections.title: THERE IS A SLGT RISK OF SVR TSTMS OVER THE NRN HIGH PLAINS
sections.text: ...THERE IS A SLGT RISK OF SVR TSTMS FROM PARTS OF THE CNTRL/SRN PLAINS EWD INTO THE PIEDMONT REGION OF THE CAROLINAS AND VA...

sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: A BROAD BELT OF CYCLONIC MID- AND HIGH-LEVEL FLOW WILL BE MAINTAINED THROUGH THE PERIOD FROM THE NWRN CONUS THROUGH THE ERN TWO-THIRDS OF THE NATION. EMBEDDED WITHIN THIS LARGE-SCALE REGIME...MORNING WATER VAPOR IMAGERY AND 12Z UPPER-AIR ANALYSIS SHOW SEVERAL IMPULSES...THE MOST NOTABLE OF WHICH BEING A STRONG SYSTEM DIGGING SEWD THROUGH B.C. INTO THE PACIFIC NW...AND OTHERS OVER THE NRN HIGH PLAINS...KS/NEB...UPPER OH VALLEY. IN ADDITION...A SERIES OF WEAK RIPPLES IN THE FLOW ARE NOTED FROM THE LOWER MS VALLEY INTO CNTRL/SRN APPALACHIANS. A LOW-LEVEL BAROCLINIC ZONE EXTENDING GENERALLY FROM THE NRN HIGH/CNTRL HIGH PLAINS SEWD THROUGH THE OZARKS INTO THE TN VALLEY/NRN GULF STATES AND THEN NEWD THROUGH THE PIEDMONT REGION WILL LIKELY SERVE AS THE FOCUS FOR STRONG/SEVERE TSTMS THROUGH THE PERIOD. ALONG AND S OF THIS BOUNDARY THE AIR MASS IS QUITE MOIST WITH DEWPOINTS IN UPPER 60S TO LOWER/MID 70S AND PW VALUES FROM 1.50 TO IN EXCESS OF TWO INCHES.

sections.title: CNTRL/SRN PLAINS EWD INTO THE MID MS VALLEY AND OZARK PLATEAU
sections.text: SHORT WAVE TROUGH CURRENTLY OVER NEB/KS WILL PROGRESS EWD WITH AN ASSOCIATED WEAK SURFACE LOW /ANALYZED OVER CNTRL KS AT 13Z/ DEVELOPING EWD TOWARD STL LATER TODAY. WHILE LOW TO MIDLEVEL WIND FIELD WILL NOT BE OVERLY STRONG...THE PRESENCE OF 50-70 KT HIGH-LEVEL FLOW IN CONJUNCTION WITH A MOIST AND UNSTABLE AIR MASS /I.E. MLCAPE OF 1500-3000 J PER KG/ WILL RESULT IN AN ENVIRONMENT SUPPORTIVE OF ORGANIZED STORMS INCLUDING SUPERCELLS CAPABLE OF LARGE HAIL...DAMAGING WINDS AND PERHAPS A TORNADO OR TWO ALONG AND SOUTH OF THE TRACK OF THE SHORT WAVE TROUGH AND SURFACE LOW. THOUGH LARGE-SCALE FORCING WILL BE WEAKER...ADDITIONAL...DIURNAL STORMS WILL BE POSSIBLE OVER THE HIGH PLAINS ALONG NNW-SSE ORIENTED SURFACE FRONT WITHIN AN ENVIRONMENT OF MODERATE CONVECTIVE INSTABILITY AND 40-45 KT OF DEEP WNWLY SHEAR. THE GIVEN ENVIRONMENT WILL SUPPORT THE DEVELOPMENT OF SEVERE STORMS...INCLUDING SUPERCELLS CAPABLE OF LARGE HAIL AND PERHAPS A COUPLE OF TORNADOES. FARTHER S...STRONG/SEVERE STORMS ARE EXPECTED TO BECOME FOCUSED LATER TODAY FROM PARTS OF THE OZARK PLATEAU EWD INTO LOWER MS VALLEY IN ADVANCE OF MCV CURRENTLY OVER CNTRL/ERN OK. THE COMBINATION OF DAYTIME HEATING AND BOUNDARY LAYER DEWPOI

sections.title: GULF COAST STATES TO SERN ATLANTIC COAST
sections.text: AS MENTIONED IN THE SYNOPSIS...SEVERAL MIDLEVEL IMPULSES ARE EVIDENT IN MORNING WATER VAPOR IMAGERY TRANSLATING GENERALLY EWD ALONG LOW-LEVEL BAROCLINIC ZONE. VISIBLE SATELLITE IMAGERY SHOWS MORE EXTENSIVE CLOUD COVER THIS MORNING ACROSS THE TN VALLEY INTO THE CNTRL/SRN APPALACHIANS. HOWEVER...AREAS TO THE S WILL LIKELY EXPERIENCE STRONG DAYTIME HEATING. WHEN COUPLED WITH LOWER/MID 70S DEWPOINTS...ENVIRONMENT WILL BECOME MODERATE TO STRONGLY UNSTABLE BY AFTERNOON. ALSO OF NOTE...12Z OBSERVED SOUNDINGS AND CURRENT VWP DATA SUGGEST A BELT OF 30-35 KT FLOW PRESENT IN THE 3-6 KM AGL LAYER...WHICH WHEN COMBINED WITH THE STRONG INSTABILITY WILL LIKELY FOSTER CORRIDORS OF MORE INTENSE STORMS...PRIMARY IN ADVANCE OF THE MORE PERSISTENT MIDLEVEL IMPULSES. THE PRIMARY HAZARD WITH THESE STORMS WILL BE DAMAGING WIND GUSTS.

sections.title: PIEDMONT AND COASTAL PLAIN
sections.text: MESOANALYSIS SHOWS A SW-NE ORIENTED BAROCLINIC ZONE SITUATED JUST E OF THE BLUE RIDGE. AIR MASS E OF THIS BOUNDARY IS QUITE MOIST WITH DEWPOINTS OF 70-75 F. VISIBLE SATELLITE IMAGERY SUGGESTS THAT INCREASING CLOUDINESS MAY TEMPER DAYTIME HEATING AND RESULTANT AIR MASS DESTABILIZATION THROUGH THE REMAINDER OF THE DAY. HOWEVER...WHERE POCKETS OF STRONG HEATING CAN OCCUR...THE PRESENCE OF THE RICH BOUNDARY LAYER MOISTURE WILL RESULT IN THE DEVELOPMENT OF MLCAPE APPROACHING 1000-2000 J/KG. A NUMBER OF MIDLEVEL IMPULSES CURRENTLY MOVING THROUGH THE CNTRL/SRN APPALACHIANS ARE EXPECTED TO CONTRIBUTE TO AN INCREASE IN STORM COVERAGE AND INTENSITY TODAY AS THE STRONGER FORCING PROGRESSIVELY OVERSPREADS THE DESTABILIZING BOUNDARY LAYER. HERE TOO...VWP DATA SHOW A BELT OF 30-40+ KT MIDLEVEL FLOW ATTENDING THESE IMPULSES. WHEN COUPLED WITH THE SLY LOW-LEVEL WIND COMPONENT...VERTICAL SHEAR PROFILES WILL BE SUPPORTIVE OF A FEW ORGANIZED/ROTATING STORMS CAPABLE OF DAMAGING WINDS AND PERHAPS A TORNADO OR TWO. PLEASE SEE MCD 1263 ON FURTHER NEAR-TERM GUIDANCE FOR THIS AREA.

sections.title: NRN HIGH PLAINS
sections.text: STRONG DYNAMIC FORCING ASSOCIATED WITH MIDLEVEL TROUGH MOVING THROUGH THE NRN INTERMOUNTAIN REGION IS EXPECTED TO SUPPORT THE DEVELOPMENT OF TSTMS ALONG COLD FRONT LATE THIS AFTERNOON INTO EVENING. FORECAST SOUNDINGS INDICATE THE PRESENCE OF STEEP LAPSE RATES AND MODEST BOUNDARY LAYER MOISTURE WHICH WILL CONTRIBUTE TO POCKETS OF MODERATE INSTABILITY. MOREOVER...VERTICAL SHEAR WILL INCREASE CONSIDERABLY IN CONCERT WITH THE ARRIVAL OF THE UPPER SYSTEM WITH ENVIRONMENT SUPPORTIVE OF HIGH-BASED SUPERCELLS AND/OR BOWING STRUCTURES CAPABLE OF DAMAGING WINDS AND HAIL. ..MEAD/GARNER.. 07/12/2010
